I study how people decide under flood risk, using surveys, simulation and LLM agents.

Illustration, not model output

It starts with a survey: what would your household do before the next flood?Household survey I designed and fielded

Agents carry those choices into the model: adapt, insure, or wait.Rule-based agents in FLOODABM · LLM agents in the WRR paper

Then the river answers. Same water, different outcomes.Drag the river, or switch adaptation off

Damage and payouts shape what each household can do next.Then the loop runs again

01 · Research

How do people decide under flood risk, and what do those decisions change?

Published · Water Resources Research, 2026

Can LLM agents stand in for households in a human–water simulation?

The paper tests large language models as the decision-making part of a human–water simulation.

Yang, Y. C. E., & Chiou, W. (2026). Water Resources Research, 62(6), e2025WR042111.

Read the paper↗Scholar record

My part

  • Co-author, second of two authors
In revision · Water Resources Research

What do household flood choices cost over time?

A coupled household and flood-catastrophe model that follows each choice through to flood damage, insurance payouts and out-of-pocket cost. The households here are rule-based agents, not LLM.

Chiou, W. Y., Yang, Y. C. E., Tanaka, T., Jamrussri, S., & Feng, S. Household Flood Adaptation and Financial Outcomes.

Read the case↗AGU25 poster

My part

  • Designed and fielded the household survey (Passaic River Basin, NJ)
  • Built the pipeline that turns survey answers into agent parameters
  • Built the coupled model, with NFIP premium, payout and deductible rules
  • First author
